title: Interface
description: One interface definition, as recorded in the Knowledge Hub. References fields by field_id rather than redefining them. This is the schema validate_oms_tms_examples.py already expected but that had not yet been written to disk.

id.description: Unique interface key. Matches either the legacy IF-### convention (IF-101) or an Andsoft-vendor convention carried through as-is (CV07_01).

protocol.description: Transport protocol, e.g. REST, MQ, SFTP, Webhook

method.description: HTTP method where applicable, e.g. POST

endpoint_url.description: URL or TBD placeholder as supplied by the vendor

owner.description: Vendor/team accountable for building and maintaining this interface (e.g. AndSoft)

spec_type.description: What kind of spec backs this entry. 'vendor-template' marks an interface documented via a vendor Word template rather than a machine-readable spec (Swagger not yet available).

response_contract.description: Short note on the response shape, e.g. 'status-code only, no structured body'

response_status_codes.description: HTTP status codes this interface's response can return, per the vendor document's own status-code table - used to generate a correct OpenAPI `responses:` block even when there's no structured JSON response body.

required_headers.description: HTTP headers the vendor document's own headers/auth table calls for (e.g. Content-Type, Authorization, X-API-Key), carried through verbatim so an ambiguous or missing authentication mechanism is visible rather than silently dropped.

field_validation_rules.description: Per-field (or per-field-group) validation rules from the vendor document's own Field/Rule/Error-code table - format constraints, error codes, and the exact business condition that triggers them.

field.description: Field name(s) as named in the vendor document - may be a comma-separated business-language list, not necessarily matching a single field_id

business_rules.description: The vendor document's own numbered business rules (e.g. BR-01) describing cross-field behaviour - when a create vs. update vs. cancel is triggered, conditional-mandatory field sets, etc. Carried as freeform text rather than modelled as fields, since these are rules about the interaction of several fields, not a single field's own definition.

flow_owner.description: Team/party operationally accountable for running and monitoring this flow day-to-day. Often the same as `owner` (the vendor/team accountable for the spec itself) until RACI ownership says otherwise - defaults to `owner` on extraction.

message_format.description: Payload format, e.g. JSON, XML, CSV, EDI. Derived from the vendor document's Content-Type where available.

volume_profile.description: Expected load for this interface. Null means the vendor document did not state this - do not default or guess a number; get it from the owning team.

deduplication_strategy.description: How duplicate/resent messages are prevented or detected. Null means not documented - check the interface's own `idempotent`/`retry_policy` values and whether any field offered as a 'key' is actually a per-message value rather than a fixed constant before filling this in.

key.description: field_id(s) that together form a safe per-message dedup key, if one genuinely exists

window.description: How long duplicates are checked against, e.g. '24h'

monitoring.description: Operational monitoring for this flow. Null means not documented - get it from the owning team rather than inventing plausible-sounding metrics.

acceptance_criteria.description: UAT sign-off criteria for this interface. Empty by default on extraction - these are drafted and agreed by humans (e.g. during promote/review), not derived from the vendor document, which doesn't state them.

test_data_ref.description: Cross-reference to this interface's test suite id in the separately-scoped Testing Hub. Null until a test suite id is assigned there - this hub does not own or duplicate test data.

io.description: Which leg of the interface this field belongs to

path.description: Dotted/bracket JSON path within the payload, e.g. shipment.orders[].pickUp.name

fixed_value.description: Set when the vendor doc specifies a constant, e.g. 'ZZ' or 'CAT2020'

source_field.description: The vendor's own source-system column name for this field, e.g. AndSoft's TMADLOCNAME, kept verbatim for traceability back to the vendor document
